root_cause.text: mac80211’s receive-side management frame validation in `ieee80211_rx_h_mgmt_check()` did not enforce the 802.11 requirement that Beacon frames use a broadcast destination address, so unicast Beacons could reach normal/beacon-protection processing and be treated as valid.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new early check in `net/mac80211/rx.c` — `if (ieee80211_is_beacon(mgmt->frame_control) && !is_broadcast_ether_addr(mgmt->da)) return RX_DROP;` — and the CVE/commit explains that previously unicast Beacons, especially with Protected Frame bit set, “would be accepted in mac80211 processing as valid Beacon frames even though they are not protected,” bypassing beacon protection.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds a new early check in `net/mac80211/rx.c` — `if (ieee80211_is_beacon(mgmt->frame_control) && !is_broadcast_ether_addr(mgmt->da)) return RX_DROP;` — and the CVE/commit explains that previously unicast Beacons, especially with Protected Frame bit set, “would be accepted in mac80211 processing as valid Beacon frames even though they are not protected,” bypassing beacon protection.

intent_record.intent_summary: Drop non-broadcast Beacon management frames early in the RX path to avoid processing invalid beacons.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in ieee80211_rx_h_mgmt_check() that detects Beacon management frames whose destination address is not broadcast and immediately returns RX_DROP, preceded by a comment indicating non-broadcast Beacon frames should be dropped.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the receive path now rejects Beacon frames addressed to anything other than the broadcast address, preventing such invalid or unexpected management frames from being processed further by later AP/beacon handling logic.

grouping_result.intent: Drop non-broadcast Beacon management frames early in the RX path to avoid processing invalid beacons.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly enforces the missing validation from the root cause by rejecting Beacon frames that are not broadcast, preventing invalid unicast Beacons from being processed as valid.

candidates.rationale: This is the beacon-specific validation path where beacon frames were accepted without additionally checking that the destination address was broadcast, allowing unicast beacons to proceed as valid.
This condition completes the pre-fix beacon handling gate, but it lacks any DA/broadcast enforcement, so beacon processing could continue for invalid unicast beacons.

vuln_statements.explanation: This beacon-specific acceptance condition lacked any check that the destination address was broadcast. As a result, unicast Beacon frames could enter normal beacon processing, which is the root cause described.

This line completes the pre-fix conditional gate for beacon handling. Because the overall condition did not include a broadcast destination-address requirement, invalid unicast Beacons were not rejected here and could be treated as valid.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the relevant management-frame validation path inside `ieee80211_rx_h_mgmt_check()`. It newly adds Beacon-specific handling: `if (rx->sdata->vif.type == NL80211_IFTYPE_AP && ieee80211_is_beacon(mgmt->frame_control) && !(rx->flags & IEEE80211_RX_BEACON_REPORTED)) { ... cfg80211_report_obss_beacon(...); ... }`. There is no check here that a Beacon's destination address is broadcast/multicast before it is reported/processed. The only subsequent validation shown is `if (!(status->rx_flags & IEEE80211_RX_RA_MATCH)) return RX_DROP_MONITOR;`, which drops only when RA does not match; that does not enforce the 802.11 Beacon DA requirement and would still allow unicast Beacons addressed to the local receiver to proceed.
